ChatPanel is built and committed in the worktree. Here's where things stand:

**Built and working** (committed as `bb6600d9` on `worktree/qf-6`):
- `ext/Chat/ChatPanel.js` — the chat log, composer and mic as one component, so the drawer and the mobile sheet will build the exact same widget instead of two hand-rolled copies.
- Its height is pure CSS (`Chat.css`'s `.chatbox-panel`): starts small, grows with content, caps at a CSS variable (`--chatbox-panel-max`), then only the log scrolls — no JS measuring.
- A new page, `ext/Chat/panel/`, shows it working: 1 message vs. 30, at sheet width and at drawer height, and the old hand-wired build (v1) right next to the new one (v2) on the same 30 messages. Screenshots proving this are in the task's `shots/` folder.
- Zero console errors / failed requests on `/framework/ext/Chat/`, `/framework/ext/Chat/panel/`, `/framework/ai2/`, and `/framework/`.

**Blocked, as the brief said to expect:** wiring `ChatPanel` into the real drawer AI tab and mobile sheet touches files (`ext/drawer/**`) that `task-mastermind-mobile-nav` still has unmerged changes in. Per the brief, I held those files and built the component first. I logged status and I'm waiting for the go-ahead from the task mastermind (it said it would relay once mobile-nav merges, estimated 30–45 minutes from ~18:22).

Everything is written up for whoever picks this back up — the open items and exactly what's left to wire are in `ext/Chat/doc/decisions.md`, and the task log (`c-chat/task.jsonl`) has the full trail.

## Summary

`ChatPanel` — the chat log, composer and mic as one component — now runs both the desktop drawer's AI tab and the mobile ✦ sheet, exactly as asked. What's live:

- **One widget, two hosts**: `ext/drawer/tabs/ai.js` and `ext/drawer/rail.js` both build `ChatPanel` now instead of separate hand-wired assemblies.
- **Variable height, pure CSS**: starts small, grows to a per-host ceiling (the drawer's own height, or the sheet's 70vh), then only the log scrolls — proven in screenshots at 1 and 30 messages, both surfaces.
- **v1 kept reachable**: `aiV1` (named export) and `DrawerRail.SheetV1` / the new `DrawerRail.SheetLinksV1` alias, plus a side-by-side v1-vs-v2 demo page at `/framework/ext/Chat/panel/`.
- **Sheet features preserved**: listens the moment it opens, each sentence still becomes its own visible bubble, and the links footer still reaches Sessions/Dictation/Settings/full AI.
- **Fixed**: the composer's text box was sizing to its placeholder instead of filling the row (`field-sizing: content` needed an explicit width) — found on the demo screenshot, fixed in `Chat.css`.
- Both new `ChatPanel(...)` call sites are marked for minion B's refine-level option.

Phase 2 is landed. Summary:

**Wired ChatPanel into production**, in the shared worktree (already committed as `4ae03642`, co-authored):
- `ext/drawer/tabs/ai.js`'s AI tab and `ext/drawer/rail.js`'s mobile ✦ sheet both now build the same `ChatPanel` — log, composer and mic as one widget. The old hand-wired builds stay reachable (`aiV1`, `DrawerRail.SheetV1`/`.SheetLinksV1`).

**Added the universal chat line** the owner asked for (`{"chat": {at, session, path, from, via, text, re}}`) to `Chat.js`: voice/typed 🎤/⌨ marks, a later `fix: true` line correcting an earlier one in place, and `place: {module, id}` for a `ux/Content` card (e.g. a Question) inline in the log — old-shape entries untouched. Documented in [ext/Chat/readme.md](http://127.0.0.1:54527/framework/ext/Chat/readme.md), demoed on [ext/Chat/'s own page](http://127.0.0.1:54527/framework/ext/Chat/).

**Proof:** the composer-width fix, plus real screenshots of the actual drawer (1920) and sheet (400) each with 1 and 30 messages, showing small→capped→scrolling — all in the task's `shots/` folder. Zero console errors on every page in this task's fence.

Landed in `c-chat/task.jsonl` with the outcome checklist; day log closed; status posted to your dev-bar log.

Both fixes are committed and verified:

1. **Via mark**: was its own row above every message (an extra line per message in a merged bubble). Now it reads inline on the sender label — "You · 🎤" — once per bubble, not once per message. `sheet-400-30msg.png` re-shot: one line per message.

2. **Composer visibility**: the drawer's panel-height ceiling was a guessed `calc(100dvh - 9rem)` that didn't leave room for the AI tab's head row and chips, so at 1920×1080 with 30 messages the composer could get scrolled out of view. Replaced the guess with a flex chain (`.drawer-ai` → `.drawer-ai-panel` → `.chatbox-panel`, each `flex: 1 1 auto; min-block-size: 0`) — the same trick already used for the mobile sheet — so real layout decides the ceiling instead of a number. Re-shot `drawer-1920-30msg.png` at the exact 1920×1080 spec: composer stays visible, only the log scrolls.

I've landed the b-refine task. Summary:

**Built and wired:**
- **[ux/Refine](/framework/ux/Refine/)** — a new class that refines rambling text at a level (clean/edit/summary), with the prompt itself editable right on the page (try your own wording on a sample, nothing saved).
- **Servex's `/api/tidy`** now takes an optional level or a custom prompt — proven byte-for-byte identical to today's behavior when neither is given.
- **`Dictate`** gained a `refine`/`on_refined` option (default off, zero change for existing callers), wired for real into the mobile assistant's mic (`ext/drawer/rail.js`, committed), and passed through from `ai2/compose.js` (inert until a sibling file, owned by another minion, forwards it).
- **The dictation playground** got two new tabs — Chunks (every Whisper resend as its own row) and Side-by-side (raw vs. refined) — plus a level picker, and a plain note that Raw is always Whisper's untouched output.
- Found and fixed a real bug along the way: a closing segment used to visibly blank for a moment before the final text landed; now it's one clean redraw.

**Left undone:** a full redesign of the `/framework/ux/Dictate/` landing page (pipeline picture, linked tiles) — that ask arrived late in the task, well past its budget, so I deferred it rather than rush a weak version. Everything it would link to already works.

Full details, proofs, and screenshots are in the task log: `public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/audio/b-refine/task.jsonl` and its `shots/` folder.

Landed. Report: [`report.md`](/framework/ai/2026-09-29/audio/d-whisper-host/report.md)

**Recommendation in short:** keep whisper-server's HTTP `/inference` as the engine — it already answers in under 100ms, well inside the ~0.9s resend budget, and is the least code to run. The real gap is the *transport*: build one websocket plugin on Servex's own dashboard (it's already the same `Server` class the dev server uses, already emits the `"http"` event a socket plugin needs, and `ws` is already a root dependency — zero new packages), so every project reaches Whisper through one socket instead of each dev server hosting its own copy. Node bindings and a child-process stream were both weighed and don't measurably beat today's approach; `whisper_streaming`'s local-agreement fix is named as the next thing worth trying only if word-splitting seams turn out to still be a real problem after the cheaper fix already shipped.

I've landed the task. Here's the summary of what was built:

## `framework/audio/` — a library of pure audio parts

Built in worktree `qf-6` (two commits, not yet merged — the task mastermind merges): six classes — **MicStream**, **MicPicker**, **LevelMeter**, **Recorder**, **PushToTalk**, **Transcriber** (Whisper + Browser engines) — each with its own page, readme, and a live "state view" (an icon with flags, a one-line row, a full data panel), plus three working assemblies: a sound recorder, a Discord-style push-to-talk stream, and mic → Whisper → text. Everything was proven headless with a fake microphone (zero console errors on every page, screenshots at 1920/400).

Two follow-ups came in mid-task from the owner (relayed by task-mastermind-audio):

1. **Every class gets a live-state view** — done fully for MicStream, Recorder and Transcriber (the three prioritized when budget got tight); MicPicker/LevelMeter/PushToTalk are logged as deferred, not silently skipped.
2. **`Transcriber.Whisper` rebuilt as a rolling local-agreement window** instead of cut-and-append — measured against the real local whisper-server with a synthesized monologue: **0 hallucinations / 0 lost words**, versus **2 hallucinations / 1 lost word** for the old cut-and-append engine (kept reachable as `Transcriber.WhisperSegments`). Full transcripts and the research on whether a real streaming server would do even better are in `doc/decisions.md` and `Transcriber/doc/streaming.md`.

One honest caveat logged: a second commit accidentally swept in an unrelated rename from a sibling minion working in the same shared worktree (0 content change, just wrong attribution — nothing lost).

I've completed this round's requests and committed the work (commit `4a7f9f1a`). Summary:

1. **Flicker proof** — a real before/after: the parent commit's code shows the caption collapsing to 0px height mid-close; this task's fix shows zero dips. Frame strip in `shots/`.
2. **Cut markers** — now visible in the Sample run ("closed — pause" / "closed — forced (15s cap)"), screenshotted.
3. **ai2 compose actually works** — `ext/Chat/Composer.js` now forwards `revise` into the real mic, so it logs a genuine revision instead of doing nothing.
4. **Renamed Refine → Revise** everywhere this task touched, carefully leaving the unrelated, pre-existing `ext/Refine/` module and `ext/Chat`'s own `refine()` concept alone.
5. **Revision logging** — ephemeral guesses/chunks stay in memory only; a finished revision now logs its own line pointing back at the raw line's id.
6. **Dictate's first screen** — one line, four linked pipeline tiles, one line each on what the five tabs show, then the live widget.
7. **Revise's page** — opens with a worked example already filled in, no API call needed to see what it does.

All required pages check clean (zero console errors/failed requests), except two pre-existing, unrelated 404s on `/framework/ai2/` for task files that don't exist in this worktree. Full details and proofs are in `public/framework/ai/2026-09-29/audio/b-refine/task.jsonl`.

## Landed

**Commit `3f155bc7`** in worktree `qf-6` (not merged — the task mastermind merges):

1. **`ux/Dictate/variants/parts/`** — a new Dictate variant that rebuilds the whisper half on `MicStream` + the rolling-window `Transcriber.Whisper`, keeping `revise:`, `on_text`, the log post, and the caption exactly as they were. It's a "pipeline" variant (overrides `start_whisper`/`on_level`/`heartbeat`/`stop`, not a look), documented as the exception to the wall's usual "never override start/stop" rule. v1 stays the default, unchanged; linked from the variants wall and one line in `ux/Dictate/readme.md`.
2. **`audio/` index** — the six parts now show as their own live row-state cards (not started, each reading idle), filling the width, with the three assemblies as bigger linked icon tiles below.
3. **`Transcriber/` page** — the icon/row/panel sizes demo now sits above the interactive demo and the `Use` code, visible on the first 1920 screen.

All five required pages (`/framework/audio/`, `/framework/audio/Transcriber/`, `/framework/ux/Dictate/`, `/framework/ux/Dictate/variants/`, and the new variant page) load with zero console errors, pass the padding check at every width, and are screenshotted at 1920 and 400 in the task's `shots/` folder.
